title: openai-compat: support tool_choice semantics, schema mapping, and tool message formatting
author: Jordan Lee
description: Motivation: the OpenAI function-calling compat layer must support the newer tool_choice semantics (when the model indicates which tool to use but also provides structured selection metadata), map OpenAI function schemas into Redwood's internal tool schema representation, and preserve tool message formatting when returning tool outputs through the OpenAI-compliant assistant messages. What this PR does (summary): - Implements tool_choice handling in the openai-compat handler so that a model replying with a tool_choice action is translated into a single tool invocation against Redwood tools. The behaviour mirrors OpenAI's semantics: tool_choice contains the chosen tool name, optional index, and a parsed set of args. - Adds schema mapping utilities to translate OpenAI-style JSON Schema (function parameters) into Redwood's ToolSchema proto-ish representation used by the runtime and toolbox registries. The mapping covers common cases (object/array/string/number/boolean, required/optional, enum, nested objects) and adds safe fallbacks for unsupported constructs (oneOf/anyOf -> union description + validation stub). - Preserves tool message formatting: tool outputs that are returned as tool messages (content, metadata) are converted to assistant messages with role "tool" and include a content_type header when present. Streaming tool outputs are forwarded as streaming assistant/tool messages so SDKs and streaming clients see partial tool output consistent with OpenAI streaming semantics. - Backwards-compatible: existing function-calling tests continue to pass. We added explicit tests for tool_choice, schema edge-cases, and message-formatting to ensure parity. - Docs and examples: updated openai-compat README to document tool_choice behaviour, schema mapping limitations, and a small migration note for customers relying on internal tool schema quirks. Implementation notes: - openai-compat/handler.go: main orchestration for parsing model responses changed to accept action.type == "tool_choice" and route to the new invoker path. The handler selects the tool by name/index and constructs a Redwood tool invocation request from the parsed args. Errors in mapping are surfaced as structured assistant messages (role="assistant", content with error details) to match OpenAI error-handling expectations. - openai-compat/schema_mapper.go: new package implementing SchemaToToolSchema(schemaJSON) -> ToolSchema mapping. The mapper is conservative: unknown/complex schema constructs are converted to a descriptive string field plus a JSON-schema fallback stored in metadata for downstream validators. - openai-compat/streaming.go: extended to stream tool messages as assistant/tool streams; added a small framing protocol to annotate frames with message_role and content_type for the SDK to restore semantics client-side. - tools/registry: small adapter to accept mapped ToolSchema when registering OpenAI-provided functions (used by the compat layer during runtime tool discovery). - sdk/python and sdk/typescript: minor adjustments to parsing tool messages coming from streaming compat responses so that the SDK exposes a unified ToolMessage type. Risks and mitigations: - Schema mismatch: mapping may lose fidelity for very complex JSON Schema features. Mitigation: mapper includes original schema in tool metadata and validation runs server-side with a non-blocking fallback to pass-through string. We documented limitations. - Streaming semantics differences between Redwood internal tools and OpenAI's streaming: added explicit tests and a framing layer; fallbacks are conservative (complete tool output will be delivered as final message). Testing: unit tests for mapper and handler, integration tests that exercise a toy model response containing tool_choice with nested args, and end-to-end smoke tests for streaming tool outputs through the compat layer. Related: references ENG-4301 (compat feature), ENG-4297 (streaming stability investigation). Checklist: - [x] Implement handler changes and mapping utilities - [x] Add unit and integration tests - [x] Update docs and examples - [x] Update SDK parsing for streaming tool messages - [x] Add migration notes Merge: squash and merge.

review_comments: Priya Natarajan: Left a couple of comments on schema_mapper.go - we should be explicit about how we handle additionalProperties and how validators will surface missing required fields. Also please add a small benchmark for mapping performance (this runs in hot path during tool registration).

Jordan Lee (author): Responded - added a short micro-benchmark and clarified additionalProperties handling (we now translate additionalProperties:true into a metadata flag and still accept arbitrary keys during runtime validation).
Ethan Morales: Question about streaming frame size limits. If tools emit very large frames, do we chunk? Suggest adding hedged IO behavior.

Jordan Lee: Answered - streaming.go now enforces a 256KB frame limit and will chunk larger tool outputs; added test for chunking. We opted not to add hedged IO in this PR to keep surface area small; tracked as ENG-4315.
Sofia Patel: Docs look good. Minor nit: migration note should call out compatibility with older SDK versions.
Jordan Lee: Updated migration doc to include SDK compatibility matrix and fallback instructions.
merge_commit: squash: openai-compat tool_choice/schema mapping and message formatting (merged by Priya Natarajan)
release_notes: Add OpenAI compat support for tool_choice, map OpenAI function schemas to Redwood ToolSchema, and preserve streaming tool message formatting. Known limitations: complex JSON Schema constructs (oneOf/anyOf) are mapped conservatively; refer to docs/migration/openai_compat_tool_choice.md for details.
